messages.subject: OOB question
parts:
Hi,
I have just starting using rattle and was hoping for some guidance
with it.

From what I understand the radomForest command uses an OOB(out-of-bag)
sample and the performance characteristic of the model can be
"validated" on the OOB sample without having to do a validation or
test set or cross validation. When i try to do this on rattle, i
believe that all i am getting is a perfect ROC curve on the training
set which is expected but not sure how to get the performance
characteristics on the OOB sample.

Am I missing something?
Thanks
Ak

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: OOB question
parts:
Hi Ak,

Rattle does not directly support plotting the ROC of the OOB scoring
from randomForest. You would need to collect the OOB predictions and
plot them using ROCR. Instead, Rattle supports a separate hold-out
dataset for the unbiased performance estimates.

The randomForest output in Rattle does include the OOB error estimate
(page 251 of the Rattle book). Also page 260 talks about the OOB error
rates.

Regards,
Graham

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: OOB question
parts:
Hi Ak,

Not all model builders use an OOB in R. Rattle allows you to use a
hold-out dataset (a test or validate dataset) for plotting unbiased
expected performance, using the same train/test/validate datasets
across different model builders.

However, as you note, predict.randomForest() returns the OOB scores
and so you can get the OOB ROC with the following (you were close!):

> crs$pr <- predict(crs$rf, type="prob")[,2]
> pred<-prediction(crs$pr, crs$dataset[crs$sample, crs$target])
> perf<- performance(pred,"tpr","fpr")
> plot(perf, col=4, add=TRUE)

This is probably an option I should work into Rattle somehow.

Regards,
Graham
